decls.statement: theorem inclusion_apply [DecidableEq α] (h : K ≤ K') (x : α) : inclusion h x = x

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.standardGeometricComplex
decls.doc:
The standard geometric simplicial complex associated to an abstract simplicial complex.

Each vertex is sent to its coordinate vector in `ι →₀ ℝ`. This is Mathlib's
`Geometry.SimplicialComplex.onFinsupp` construction.
decls.statement:
def standardGeometricComplex (K : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι) :
    Geometry.SimplicialComplex ℝ (ι →₀ ℝ)

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.Realization
decls.doc: The carrier of the geometric realization (polyhedron) of an abstract simplicial complex.
decls.statement: abbrev Realization (K : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι) : Type _

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.StandardSimplex
decls.doc: The closed simplex spanned by a finite vertex set, in standard barycentric coordinates.
decls.statement: abbrev StandardSimplex (σ : Finset ι) : Type _

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.instTopologicalSpaceStandardSimplex
decls.doc:
The topology induced by the coordinatewise topology on `ι → ℝ`. These are the domain
topologies used to define the weak topology on the whole realization.
decls.statement: instance (σ : Finset ι) : TopologicalSpace (StandardSimplex σ)

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.mem_standardGeometricComplex_faces_iff
decls.doc: A geometric face is exactly the image of an abstract face under the coordinate embedding.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_standardGeometricComplex_faces_iff (K : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι)
    (τ : Finset (ι →₀ ℝ)) :
    τ ∈ (standardGeometricComplex K).faces ↔
      ∃ σ ∈ K, σ.image (fun v => Finsupp.single v (1 : ℝ)) = τ

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.faceInclusion
decls.doc: Include the realization of a face into the whole polyhedron.
decls.statement:
def faceInclusion (K : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι) (σ : Face K) :
    StandardSimplex σ.1 → Realization K

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.faceInclusion_val
decls.doc: A face inclusion does not change the underlying barycentric coordinates.
decls.statement:
theorem faceInclusion_val (K : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι) (σ : Face K)
    (x : StandardSimplex σ.1) :
    (faceInclusion K σ x : ι →₀ ℝ) = x

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.instTopologicalSpaceRealization
decls.doc: The weak topology on a realization, final with respect to all face inclusions.
decls.statement: instance (K : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι) : TopologicalSpace (Realization K)

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.continuous_faceInclusion
decls.doc: Every face inclusion is continuous for the weak topology on the realization.
decls.statement:
theorem continuous_faceInclusion (K : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι) (σ : Face K) :
    Continuous (faceInclusion K σ)

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.continuous_iff_faceInclusion
decls.doc:
A map out of a realization is continuous exactly when its restriction to every face is
continuous.

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.image_single_mem_standardGeometricComplex_faces
decls.doc: The coordinate image of every abstract face is a face of the geometric complex.

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.mem_realization_iff
decls.doc:
A point belongs to the standard polyhedron exactly when it lies in the convex hull of the
coordinate image of some abstract face.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_realization_iff {K : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι} {x : ι →₀ ℝ} :
    x ∈ (standardGeometricComplex K).space ↔
      ∃ σ ∈ K, x ∈
        convexHull ℝ (σ.image (fun v => Finsupp.single v (1 : ℝ)) : Set (ι →₀ ℝ))

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.StandardSimplex.nonneg
decls.doc: Barycentric coordinates in a standard simplex are nonnegative.
decls.statement:
theorem StandardSimplex.nonneg {σ : Finset ι} (x : StandardSimplex σ) (v : ι) :
    0 ≤ x.1 v

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.StandardSimplex.sum_eq_one
decls.doc: The barycentric coordinates in a standard simplex sum to one.
decls.statement:
theorem StandardSimplex.sum_eq_one {σ : Finset ι} (x : StandardSimplex σ) :
    x.1.sum (fun _ r => r) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.StandardSimplex.support_subset
decls.doc: The support of a point in a standard simplex is contained in its vertex set.
decls.statement:
theorem StandardSimplex.support_subset {σ : Finset ι} (x : StandardSimplex σ) :
    x.1.support ⊆ σ

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.mem_standardSimplex_iff
decls.doc: Membership in a standard simplex in terms of barycentric coordinates.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_standardSimplex_iff {σ : Finset ι} {x : ι →₀ ℝ} :
    x ∈ convexHull ℝ
        ((fun v => Finsupp.single v (1 : ℝ)) '' (σ : Set ι)) ↔
      (∀ v, 0 ≤ x v) ∧ x.sum (fun _ r => r) = 1 ∧ x.support ⊆ σ

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.StandardSimplex.mem_convexHull_support
decls.doc: A point of a standard simplex lies in the simplex spanned by its support.
decls.statement:
theorem StandardSimplex.mem_convexHull_support {σ : Finset ι} (x : StandardSimplex σ) :
    x.1 ∈ convexHull ℝ
      (x.1.support.image (fun v => Finsupp.single v (1 : ℝ)) : Set (ι →₀ ℝ))

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.support_mem
decls.doc: The support of a realization point is an abstract face.
decls.statement: theorem support_mem (K : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι) (x : Realization K) : x.1.support ∈ K

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.carrier
decls.doc: The minimal abstract face carrying a point of the realization.
decls.statement: def carrier (K : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι) (x : Realization K) : Face K

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.carrier_val
decls.doc: The vertices of the carrier are exactly the nonzero barycentric coordinates.
decls.statement:
theorem carrier_val (K : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι) (x : Realization K) :
    (carrier K x).1 = x.1.support

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.mem_convexHull_carrier
decls.doc: A realization point belongs to the closed simplex spanned by its carrier.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_convexHull_carrier (K : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι) (x : Realization K) :
    x.1 ∈ convexHull ℝ
      ((carrier K x).1.image (fun v => Finsupp.single v (1 : ℝ)) : Set (ι →₀ ℝ))

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.carrier_minimal
decls.doc: The carrier is contained in every finite vertex set whose closed simplex contains the point.
decls.statement:
theorem carrier_minimal (K : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι) (x : Realization K) {σ : Finset ι}
    (hx : x.1 ∈ convexHull ℝ
      (σ.image (fun v => Finsupp.single v (1 : ℝ)) : Set (ι →₀ ℝ))) :
    (carrier K x).1 ⊆ σ

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.single_mem_standardGeometricComplex_space
decls.doc: The standard coordinate vector of every vertex belongs to the geometric realization.
decls.statement:
theorem single_mem_standardGeometricComplex_space (K : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι) (v : ι) :
    Finsupp.single v 1 ∈ (standardGeometricComplex K).space

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.vertex
decls.doc: The canonical point of the geometric realization corresponding to a vertex.
decls.statement: def vertex (K : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι) (v : ι) : Realization K

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.vertex_val
decls.doc: The underlying finitely supported function of a realization vertex is its coordinate vector.
decls.statement:
theorem vertex_val (K : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι) (v : ι) :
    (vertex K v : ι →₀ ℝ) = Finsupp.single v 1

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.vertex_injective
decls.doc: Distinct vertices give distinct points in the geometric realization.
decls.statement:
theorem vertex_injective (K : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι) :
    Function.Injective (vertex K)

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.vertexEmbedding
decls.doc: The canonical map from vertices to the realization.
decls.statement: def vertexEmbedding (K : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι) : ι ↪ Realization K

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.vertexEmbedding_apply
decls.doc: The vertex embedding sends a vertex to its canonical point in the realization.
decls.statement:
theorem vertexEmbedding_apply (K : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι) (v : ι) :
    vertexEmbedding K v = vertex K v

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.vertex_bot_surjective
decls.doc: The vertices exhaust the realization of the bottom abstract simplicial complex.
decls.statement:
theorem vertex_bot_surjective :
    Function.Surjective (vertex (⊥ : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι))

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.realizationBotDiscreteTopology
decls.doc: The weak topology on the realization of the bottom abstract simplicial complex is discrete.
decls.statement:
instance realizationBotDiscreteTopology :
    DiscreteTopology (Realization (⊥ : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι))

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.vertexEquivBot
decls.statement:
def vertexEquivBot :
    ι ≃ Realization (⊥ : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι)

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.realizationBotHomeomorph
decls.doc:
The realization of the bottom abstract simplicial complex is canonically homeomorphic to its
vertex type equipped with a discrete topology.
decls.statement:
def realizationBotHomeomorph [TopologicalSpace ι] [DiscreteTopology ι] :
    Realization (⊥ : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι) ≃ₜ ι

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.realizationBotHomeomorph_symm_apply
decls.doc:
Under the canonical homeomorphism for the bottom complex, the inverse sends a vertex to its
standard barycentric point.
decls.statement:
theorem realizationBotHomeomorph_symm_apply [TopologicalSpace ι] [DiscreteTopology ι] (v : ι) :
    (realizationBotHomeomorph (ι := ι)).symm v =
      vertex (⊥ : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι) v

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.realizationBotHomeomorph_apply_vertex
decls.doc: The canonical homeomorphism sends the barycentric point of a vertex back to that vertex.
decls.statement:
theorem realizationBotHomeomorph_apply_vertex [TopologicalSpace ι] [DiscreteTopology ι] (v : ι) :
    realizationBotHomeomorph (vertex (⊥ : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι) v) = v

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.standardGeometricComplex_space_mono
decls.doc: Inclusion of abstract complexes induces inclusion of their standard polyhedra.
decls.statement:
theorem standardGeometricComplex_space_mono {K L : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι} (hKL : K ≤ L) :
    (standardGeometricComplex K).space ⊆ (standardGeometricComplex L).space

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.realizationMap
decls.doc: The continuous map of realizations induced by an inclusion of abstract complexes.
decls.statement:
def realizationMap {K L : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι} (hKL : K ≤ L) :
    Realization K → Realization L

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.realizationMap_val
decls.doc: An induced map of realizations does not change the underlying barycentric coordinates.
decls.statement:
theorem realizationMap_val {K L : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι} (hKL : K ≤ L)
    (x : Realization K) :
    (realizationMap hKL x : ι →₀ ℝ) = x

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.realizationMap_injective
decls.doc: The map of realizations induced by an inclusion is injective.
decls.statement:
theorem realizationMap_injective {K L : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι} (hKL : K ≤ L) :
    Function.Injective (realizationMap hKL)

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.realizationMap_comp_faceInclusion
decls.doc:
An inclusion map restricted to a face is the corresponding face inclusion in the larger
complex.
decls.statement:
theorem realizationMap_comp_faceInclusion {K L : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι} (hKL : K ≤ L)
    (σ : Face K) :
    realizationMap hKL ∘ faceInclusion K σ = faceInclusion L ⟨σ.1, hKL σ.2⟩

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.continuous_realizationMap
decls.doc: The map of realizations induced by an inclusion is continuous.
decls.statement:
theorem continuous_realizationMap {K L : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι} (hKL : K ≤ L) :
    Continuous (realizationMap hKL)

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.realizationMap_refl
decls.doc: The map induced by the reflexive inclusion is the identity.
decls.statement:
theorem realizationMap_refl (K : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι) :
    realizationMap (le_refl K) = id

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.realizationMap_trans
decls.doc: Maps induced by inclusions compose according to transitivity of inclusion.
decls.statement:
theorem realizationMap_trans {K L M : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι} (hKL : K ≤ L) (hLM : L ≤ M) :
    realizationMap (hKL.trans hLM) = realizationMap hLM ∘ realizationMap hKL

decls.name: TauCeti.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.simplex
decls.doc: The abstract simplex spanned by `V`: its faces are the nonempty subsets of `V`.
decls.statement: def simplex (V : Finset ι) : _root_.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex ι

decls.name: TauCeti.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.simplexBoundary
decls.doc:
The boundary of the abstract simplex spanned by `V`: its faces are the nonempty proper
subsets of `V`.
decls.statement: def simplexBoundary (V : Finset ι) : _root_.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex ι

decls.name: TauCeti.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.mem_simplex
decls.doc:
A finite set is a face of a simplex exactly when it is nonempty and contained in the
spanning vertex set.
decls.statement: theorem mem_simplex : σ ∈ simplex V ↔ σ.Nonempty ∧ σ ⊆ V

decls.name: TauCeti.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.mem_simplexBoundary
decls.doc:
A finite set is a face of a simplex boundary exactly when it is a nonempty proper subset of
the spanning vertex set.
decls.statement: theorem mem_simplexBoundary : σ ∈ simplexBoundary V ↔ σ.Nonempty ∧ σ ⊂ V

decls.name: TauCeti.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.self_mem_simplex
decls.doc: The spanning vertex set is a face of its simplex exactly when it is nonempty.
decls.statement: theorem self_mem_simplex : V ∈ simplex V ↔ V.Nonempty

decls.name: TauCeti.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.self_notMem_simplexBoundary
decls.doc: The spanning vertex set is not a face of its own boundary.
decls.statement: theorem self_notMem_simplexBoundary : V ∉ simplexBoundary V

decls.name: TauCeti.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.singleton_mem_simplex
decls.doc: A vertex belongs to the spanning set exactly when its singleton is a face of the simplex.
decls.statement: theorem singleton_mem_simplex {v : ι} : {v} ∈ simplex V ↔ v ∈ V

decls.name: TauCeti.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.finite_faces_simplex
decls.doc: An abstract simplex has finitely many faces: they are subsets of the spanning set.
decls.statement: theorem finite_faces_simplex (V : Finset ι) : (simplex V).faces.Finite

decls.name: TauCeti.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.isCone_simplex
decls.doc: An abstract simplex is a cone with apex any of its vertices.
decls.statement: theorem isCone_simplex [DecidableEq ι] {v : ι} (hv : v ∈ V) : IsCone (simplex V) v

decls.name: TauCeti.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.singleton_mem_simplexBoundary
decls.doc:
A singleton is a boundary face exactly when its vertex belongs to a spanning set containing
at least one other vertex.
decls.statement:
theorem singleton_mem_simplexBoundary {v : ι} :
    {v} ∈ simplexBoundary V ↔ v ∈ V ∧ V ≠ {v}

decls.name: TauCeti.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.simplexBoundary_le_simplex
decls.doc: The boundary is a subcomplex of the simplex.
decls.statement: theorem simplexBoundary_le_simplex : simplexBoundary V ≤ simplex V

decls.name: TauCeti.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.simplexBoundary_lt_simplex
decls.doc: The boundary of a simplex with nonempty spanning set is a strict subcomplex of the simplex.
decls.statement: theorem simplexBoundary_lt_simplex (hV : V.Nonempty) : simplexBoundary V < simplex V

decls.name: TauCeti.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.simplex_empty
decls.doc: The simplex on the empty spanning set has no faces.
decls.statement: theorem simplex_empty : simplex (∅ : Finset ι) = ⊥

decls.name: TauCeti.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.simplexBoundary_empty
decls.doc: The boundary of the empty simplex has no faces.
decls.statement: theorem simplexBoundary_empty : simplexBoundary (∅ : Finset ι) = ⊥

decls.name: TauCeti.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.simplexBoundary_singleton
decls.doc: The boundary of a one-vertex simplex is empty.
decls.statement: theorem simplexBoundary_singleton (v : ι) : simplexBoundary {v} = ⊥

decls.name: TauCeti.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.simplex_univ
decls.doc: The simplex on all vertices is the top pre-abstract simplicial complex.
decls.statement: theorem simplex_univ [Fintype ι] : simplex (Finset.univ : Finset ι) = ⊤

decls.name: TauCeti.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.simplexBoundary_univ_fin_two
decls.doc:
The boundary of the standard one-simplex consists of its two vertices. Equivalently, it is
the underlying precomplex of the bottom abstract simplicial complex on `Fin 2`.
decls.statement:
theorem simplexBoundary_univ_fin_two :
    simplexBoundary (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin 2)) =
      (⊥ : AbstractSimplicialComplex (Fin 2)).toPreAbstractSimplicialComplex

decls.name: TauCeti.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.simplex_le_iff
decls.doc:
The simplex on `V` is contained in a complex exactly when `V` is a face of the complex
whenever `V` is nonempty.  For `V = ∅` the simplex is `⊥`, so it is contained in every complex.
decls.statement: theorem simplex_le_iff : simplex V ≤ K ↔ (V.Nonempty → V ∈ K)

decls.name: TauCeti.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.simplex_le_simplex_iff
decls.doc: Simplices are ordered exactly when their spanning vertex sets are ordered.
decls.statement: theorem simplex_le_simplex_iff : simplex V ≤ simplex W ↔ V ⊆ W

decls.name: TauCeti.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.simplex_mono
decls.doc: Enlarging the spanning vertex set enlarges the simplex.
decls.statement: theorem simplex_mono (h : V ⊆ W) : simplex V ≤ simplex W

decls.name: TauCeti.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.simplexBoundary_mono
decls.doc: Enlarging the spanning vertex set enlarges the boundary.
decls.statement: theorem simplexBoundary_mono (h : V ⊆ W) : simplexBoundary V ≤ simplexBoundary W

decls.name: TauCeti.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.mem_simplexBoundary_iff_mem_simplex_ne
decls.doc: A face of a simplex lies in its boundary exactly when it is not the whole spanning set.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_simplexBoundary_iff_mem_simplex_ne :
    σ ∈ simplexBoundary V ↔ σ ∈ simplex V ∧ σ ≠ V

decls.name: TauCeti.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.mem_simplex_iff_mem_simplexBoundary_or_eq
decls.doc:
The faces of a simplex are its boundary faces together with the spanning set itself, the
latter only when the spanning set is nonempty.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_simplex_iff_mem_simplexBoundary_or_eq :
    σ ∈ simplex V ↔ σ ∈ simplexBoundary V ∨ V.Nonempty ∧ σ = V

decls.name: TauCeti.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.closedStar_simplex
decls.doc: The closed star of any subset `σ ⊆ V` in the simplex on `V` is the entire simplex.
decls.statement: theorem closedStar_simplex (hσ : σ ⊆ V) : closedStar (simplex V) σ = simplex V

decls.name: TauCeti.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.link_simplex
decls.doc:
The link of any subset `σ ⊆ V` in the simplex on `V` is the simplex on the vertices of `V`
not in `σ`.
decls.statement: theorem link_simplex (hσ : σ ⊆ V) : link (simplex V) σ = simplex (V \ σ)

decls.name: TauCeti.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.deletion_simplex_self
decls.doc: Deleting the full vertex set from a simplex leaves exactly its boundary.
decls.statement: theorem deletion_simplex_self : deletion (simplex V) V = simplexBoundary V

decls.name: TauCeti.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.mem_closedStar_simplexBoundary
decls.doc:
A set `ρ` lies in the closed star of `σ` in the boundary of the simplex on `V` exactly when
`ρ` is nonempty and `ρ ∪ σ` is a proper subset of `V`.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_closedStar_simplexBoundary {ρ : Finset ι} :
    ρ ∈ closedStar (simplexBoundary V) σ ↔ ρ.Nonempty ∧ ρ ∪ σ ⊂ V

decls.name: TauCeti.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.link_simplexBoundary
decls.doc:
The link of any subset `σ ⊆ V` in the boundary of the simplex on `V` is the boundary of the
simplex on the complementary vertices.
decls.statement:
theorem link_simplexBoundary (hσ : σ ⊆ V) :
    link (simplexBoundary V) σ = simplexBoundary (V \ σ)

decls.name: TauCeti.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.link_simplex_self
decls.doc:
The link of the full vertex set in its simplex is empty.  (`simp` also proves this via
`link_simplex`; the named form is kept for convenience.)
decls.statement: theorem link_simplex_self : link (simplex V) V = ⊥

decls.name: TauCeti.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.link_simplexBoundary_self
decls.doc:
The link of the full vertex set `V` in the boundary of the simplex on `V` is empty (note `V`
itself is not a face of that boundary).  The statement also covers the empty spanning set.
(`simp` also proves this via `link_simplexBoundary`; the named form is kept for convenience.)
decls.statement: theorem link_simplexBoundary_self : link (simplexBoundary V) V = ⊥

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.univ_mem_top
decls.statement:
theorem univ_mem_top :
    (Finset.univ : Finset ι) ∈ (⊤ : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι)

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.topFace
decls.statement: def topFace : Face (⊤ : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι)

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.realizationTopHomeomorphStdSimplex
decls.doc:
The realization of the full abstract complex on a finite vertex type is homeomorphic to
Mathlib's standard simplex of nonnegative coordinate functions summing to one.
decls.statement:
def realizationTopHomeomorphStdSimplex :
    Realization (⊤ : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι) ≃ₜ stdSimplex ℝ ι

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.realizationTopHomeomorphStdSimplex_apply
decls.doc: The full-complex realization homeomorphism reads the same barycentric coordinates.
decls.statement:
theorem realizationTopHomeomorphStdSimplex_apply (x : Realization
    (⊤ : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι)) (i : ι) :
    realizationTopHomeomorphStdSimplex x i = x.1 i

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.realizationTopHomeomorphStdSimplex_symm_apply_val
decls.doc:
The inverse full-complex realization homeomorphism has the prescribed barycentric
coordinates.
decls.statement:
theorem realizationTopHomeomorphStdSimplex_symm_apply_val (x : stdSimplex ℝ ι) (i : ι) :
    (realizationTopHomeomorphStdSimplex.symm x : ι →₀ ℝ) i = x i

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.realizationOneSimplexHomeomorphUnitInterval
decls.doc:
The realization of the standard one-simplex is homeomorphic to the unit interval. The zeroth
vertex maps to `0` and the first vertex maps to `1`; see the two endpoint lemmas below.
decls.statement:
def realizationOneSimplexHomeomorphUnitInterval :
    Realization (⊤ : AbstractSimplicialComplex (Fin 2)) ≃ₜ unitInterval

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.stdSimplexHomeomorphUnitInterval_apply
decls.statement:
theorem stdSimplexHomeomorphUnitInterval_apply (x : stdSimplex ℝ (Fin 2)) :
    (stdSimplexHomeomorphUnitInterval x : ℝ) = x 1

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.stdSimplexHomeomorphUnitInterval_symm_apply
decls.statement:
theorem stdSimplexHomeomorphUnitInterval_symm_apply (x : unitInterval) :
    (stdSimplexHomeomorphUnitInterval.symm x : Fin 2 → ℝ) =
      ![1 - (x : ℝ), (x : ℝ)]

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.realizationOneSimplexHomeomorphUnitInterval_coe
decls.doc: The one-simplex homeomorphism is its second barycentric coordinate.
decls.statement:
theorem realizationOneSimplexHomeomorphUnitInterval_coe (x : Realization
    (⊤ : AbstractSimplicialComplex (Fin 2))) :
    (realizationOneSimplexHomeomorphUnitInterval x : ℝ) = x.1 1

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.realizationOneSimplexHomeomorphUnitInterval_symm_apply_val_zero
decls.doc:
The zeroth barycentric coordinate of the interval inverse is one minus the interval
coordinate.
decls.statement:
theorem realizationOneSimplexHomeomorphUnitInterval_symm_apply_val_zero (x : unitInterval) :
    (realizationOneSimplexHomeomorphUnitInterval.symm x : Fin 2 →₀ ℝ) 0 =
      1 - (x : ℝ)

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.realizationOneSimplexHomeomorphUnitInterval_symm_apply_val_one
decls.doc: The first barycentric coordinate of the interval inverse is the interval coordinate.
decls.statement:
theorem realizationOneSimplexHomeomorphUnitInterval_symm_apply_val_one (x : unitInterval) :
    (realizationOneSimplexHomeomorphUnitInterval.symm x : Fin 2 →₀ ℝ) 1 = (x : ℝ)

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.realizationOneSimplexHomeomorphUnitInterval_vertex_zero
decls.doc: The zeroth vertex of the realized one-simplex is the left endpoint of the interval.
decls.statement:
theorem realizationOneSimplexHomeomorphUnitInterval_vertex_zero :
    realizationOneSimplexHomeomorphUnitInterval
      (vertex (⊤ : AbstractSimplicialComplex (Fin 2)) 0) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.realizationOneSimplexHomeomorphUnitInterval_vertex_one
decls.doc: The first vertex of the realized one-simplex is the right endpoint of the interval.
decls.statement:
theorem realizationOneSimplexHomeomorphUnitInterval_vertex_one :
    realizationOneSimplexHomeomorphUnitInterval
      (vertex (⊤ : AbstractSimplicialComplex (Fin 2)) 1) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.finTwoEquivSphereZero
decls.statement: def finTwoEquivSphereZero : Fin 2 ≃ sphere (0 : ℝ) 1

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.finTwoHomeomorphSphereZero
decls.statement: def finTwoHomeomorphSphereZero : Fin 2 ≃ₜ sphere (0 : ℝ) 1

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.finTwoHomeomorphSphereZero_zero
decls.statement:
theorem finTwoHomeomorphSphereZero_zero :
    (finTwoHomeomorphSphereZero 0 : ℝ) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.finTwoHomeomorphSphereZero_one
decls.statement:
theorem finTwoHomeomorphSphereZero_one :
    (finTwoHomeomorphSphereZero 1 : ℝ) = -1

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.realizationOneSimplexBoundaryHomeomorphSphereZero
decls.doc:
The realization of the boundary of the standard one-simplex is homeomorphic to the unit
zero-sphere. By `simplexBoundary_univ_fin_two`, the underlying precomplex of the source is exactly
the boundary of the simplex on the two vertices.
decls.statement:
def realizationOneSimplexBoundaryHomeomorphSphereZero :
    Realization (⊥ : AbstractSimplicialComplex (Fin 2)) ≃ₜ sphere (0 : ℝ) 1

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.realizationOneSimplexBoundaryHomeomorphSphereZero_vertex_zero
decls.doc: The zeroth boundary vertex maps to `1` on the zero-sphere.
decls.statement:
theorem realizationOneSimplexBoundaryHomeomorphSphereZero_vertex_zero :
    (realizationOneSimplexBoundaryHomeomorphSphereZero
      (vertex (⊥ : AbstractSimplicialComplex (Fin 2)) 0) : ℝ) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.realizationOneSimplexBoundaryHomeomorphSphereZero_vertex_one
decls.doc: The first boundary vertex maps to `-1` on the zero-sphere.
decls.statement:
theorem realizationOneSimplexBoundaryHomeomorphSphereZero_vertex_one :
    (realizationOneSimplexBoundaryHomeomorphSphereZero
      (vertex (⊥ : AbstractSimplicialComplex (Fin 2)) 1) : ℝ) = -1

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.realizationOneSimplexBoundaryHomeomorphSphereZero_symm_apply_one
decls.doc: The inverse zero-sphere homeomorphism sends `1` to the zeroth boundary vertex.
decls.statement:
theorem realizationOneSimplexBoundaryHomeomorphSphereZero_symm_apply_one :
    realizationOneSimplexBoundaryHomeomorphSphereZero.symm ⟨1, by simp⟩ =
      vertex (⊥ : AbstractSimplicialComplex (Fin 2)) 0

decls.name: TauCeti.AbstractSimplicialComplex.realizationOneSimplexBoundaryHomeomorphSphereZero_symm_apply_neg_one
decls.doc: The inverse zero-sphere homeomorphism sends `-1` to the first boundary vertex.
decls.statement:
theorem realizationOneSimplexBoundaryHomeomorphSphereZero_symm_apply_neg_one :
    realizationOneSimplexBoundaryHomeomorphSphereZero.symm ⟨-1, by simp⟩ =
      vertex (⊥ : AbstractSimplicialComplex (Fin 2)) 1

decls.name: TauCeti.UniversalCover.instSMulFundamentalGroup
decls.doc: The fundamental group acts on the universal cover by prepending the inverse loop class.
decls.statement: instance : SMul (FundamentalGroup X x₀) (UniversalCover x₀)

decls.name: TauCeti.UniversalCover.smul_mk
decls.doc: The fundamental-group action prepends the inverse loop class to a representative path.
decls.statement:
theorem smul_mk (g : FundamentalGroup X x₀) (x : X)
    (q : Path.Homotopic.Quotient x₀ x) :
    g • mk x q = mk x (g⁻¹.toPath.trans q)

decls.name: TauCeti.UniversalCover.inv_smul_mk
decls.doc: Acting by an inverse prepends the corresponding loop class without an inverse.
decls.statement:
theorem inv_smul_mk (g : FundamentalGroup X x₀) (x : X)
    (q : Path.Homotopic.Quotient x₀ x) :
    g⁻¹ • mk x q = mk x (g.toPath.trans q)

decls.name: TauCeti.UniversalCover.proj_smul
decls.doc: The fundamental-group action preserves the endpoint projection.
decls.statement:
theorem proj_smul (g : FundamentalGroup X x₀) (p : UniversalCover x₀) :
    proj (g • p) = proj p

decls.name: TauCeti.UniversalCover.instMulActionFundamentalGroup
decls.doc: The action of the fundamental group on the universal cover.
decls.statement: instance : MulAction (FundamentalGroup X x₀) (UniversalCover x₀)

decls.name: TauCeti.UniversalCover.instFaithfulSMulFundamentalGroup
decls.doc: The action on the universal cover is faithful.
decls.statement: instance : FaithfulSMul (FundamentalGroup X x₀) (UniversalCover x₀)

decls.name: TauCeti.UniversalCover.instContinuousConstSMulFundamentalGroup
decls.doc: Every fundamental-group element acts continuously on the universal cover.
decls.statement: instance : ContinuousConstSMul (FundamentalGroup X x₀) (UniversalCover x₀)

decls.name: TauCeti.UniversalCover.instIsCancelSMulFundamentalGroup
decls.doc: The action of the fundamental group on the universal cover is free.
decls.statement: instance : IsCancelSMul (FundamentalGroup X x₀) (UniversalCover x₀)

decls.name: TauCeti.UniversalCover.proj_eq_iff_mem_orbit
decls.doc:
Two points of the universal cover have the same projection exactly when they lie in the
same fundamental-group orbit.
decls.statement:
theorem proj_eq_iff_mem_orbit {p₁ p₂ : UniversalCover x₀} :
    proj p₁ = proj p₂ ↔ p₁ ∈ MulAction.orbit (FundamentalGroup X x₀) p₂

decls.name: TauCeti.UniversalCover.proj_surjective
decls.doc: The endpoint projection is surjective when the base is path-connected.
decls.statement:
theorem proj_surjective [PathConnectedSpace X] :
    Function.Surjective (proj : UniversalCover x₀ → X)

decls.name: TauCeti.UniversalCover.isQuotientCoveringMap
decls.doc: The endpoint projection is a quotient covering map for the fundamental-group action.
decls.statement:
theorem isQuotientCoveringMap
    [LocallyPathConnectedSpace X] [PathConnectedSpace X]
    [SemilocallySimplyConnectedSpace X] :
    IsQuotientCoveringMap (proj : UniversalCover x₀ → X) (FundamentalGroup X x₀)

decls.name: TauCeti.Deck.mem_addCircleCoe
decls.doc:
A homeomorphism of `𝕜` is a deck transformation of `(↑) : 𝕜 → AddCircle p` exactly when it
moves every point within the period subgroup `zmultiples p`.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_addCircleCoe {φ : 𝕜 ≃ₜ 𝕜} :
    φ ∈ Deck ((↑) : 𝕜 → AddCircle p) ↔ ∀ e, φ e - e ∈ zmultiples p

decls.name: TauCeti.Deck.addRightZMultiples
decls.doc:
Right translation by an element of `zmultiples p`, as a deck transformation of
`(↑) : 𝕜 → AddCircle p`.
decls.statement: def addRightZMultiples (a : zmultiples p) : Deck ((↑) : 𝕜 → AddCircle p)

decls.name: TauCeti.Deck.addRightZMultiples_apply
decls.statement:
theorem addRightZMultiples_apply (a : zmultiples p) (e : 𝕜) :
    (addRightZMultiples a).1 e = e + (a : 𝕜)

decls.name: TauCeti.Deck.addRightZMultiples_zero
decls.statement: theorem addRightZMultiples_zero : addRightZMultiples (0 : zmultiples p) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.Deck.addRightZMultiples_add
decls.statement:
theorem addRightZMultiples_add (a b : zmultiples p) :
    addRightZMultiples (a + b) = addRightZMultiples a * addRightZMultiples b

decls.name: TauCeti.Deck.addRightZMultiples_injective
decls.statement:
theorem addRightZMultiples_injective :
    Function.Injective (addRightZMultiples : zmultiples p → Deck ((↑) : 𝕜 → AddCircle p))

decls.name: TauCeti.Deck.isRegular_addCircleCoe
decls.doc:
The projection `(↑) : 𝕜 → AddCircle p` has regular deck action: it is surjective and its
deck transformation group acts transitively on every fibre.
decls.statement: theorem isRegular_addCircleCoe : IsRegular ((↑) : 𝕜 → AddCircle p)

decls.name: TauCeti.Deck.addCircleCoe_eq_add_apply_zero
decls.doc:
On a preconnected domain with totally disconnected period subgroup, a deck transformation of
`(↑) : 𝕜 → AddCircle p` is right translation by `φ 0`.
decls.statement:
theorem addCircleCoe_eq_add_apply_zero [PreconnectedSpace 𝕜]
    [TotallyDisconnectedSpace (zmultiples p)] (φ : Deck ((↑) : 𝕜 → AddCircle p)) (e : 𝕜) :
    φ.1 e = e + φ.1 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Deck.addRightZMultiplesHom
decls.doc:
Right translation by elements of the period subgroup, as a monoid homomorphism from the
multiplicatively written `zmultiples p` to the deck transformation group of
`(↑) : 𝕜 → AddCircle p`. This bundles `addRightZMultiples`.
decls.statement:
def addRightZMultiplesHom :
    Multiplicative (zmultiples p) →* Deck ((↑) : 𝕜 → AddCircle p)

decls.name: TauCeti.Deck.addRightZMultiplesHom_apply
decls.statement:
theorem addRightZMultiplesHom_apply (a : Multiplicative (zmultiples p)) :
    addRightZMultiplesHom a = addRightZMultiples a.toAdd

decls.name: TauCeti.Deck.addCircleMulEquiv
decls.doc:
The deck transformation group of `(↑) : 𝕜 → AddCircle p` on a preconnected domain with
totally disconnected period subgroup is the group of translations by the period subgroup.
decls.statement:
def addCircleMulEquiv [PreconnectedSpace 𝕜]
    [TotallyDisconnectedSpace (zmultiples p)] :
    Multiplicative (zmultiples p) ≃* Deck ((↑) : 𝕜 → AddCircle p)

decls.name: TauCeti.Deck.addCircleMulEquiv_apply
decls.statement:
theorem addCircleMulEquiv_apply [PreconnectedSpace 𝕜] [TotallyDisconnectedSpace (zmultiples p)]
    (a : Multiplicative (zmultiples p)) :
    addCircleMulEquiv a = addRightZMultiples a.toAdd

decls.name: TauCeti.Deck.addCircleMulEquiv_symm_apply_coe
decls.statement:
theorem addCircleMulEquiv_symm_apply_coe [PreconnectedSpace 𝕜]
    [TotallyDisconnectedSpace (zmultiples p)] (φ : Deck ((↑) : 𝕜 → AddCircle p)) :
    ((addCircleMulEquiv.symm φ).toAdd : 𝕜) = φ.1 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Deck.addCircleMulEquivInt
decls.doc:
For a non-torsion period, the deck transformation group of the quotient map
`(↑) : 𝕜 → AddCircle p` on a preconnected domain with totally disconnected period subgroup is
infinite cyclic: `Multiplicative ℤ`. In the standard real covering case this is the deck group
of the universal cover `ℝ → S¹`.
decls.statement:
def addCircleMulEquivInt [PreconnectedSpace 𝕜]
    [TotallyDisconnectedSpace (zmultiples p)] (hp : ¬ IsOfFinAddOrder p) :
    Multiplicative ℤ ≃* Deck ((↑) : 𝕜 → AddCircle p)

decls.name: TauCeti.Deck.addCircleMulEquivInt_apply
decls.statement:
theorem addCircleMulEquivInt_apply [PreconnectedSpace 𝕜]
    [TotallyDisconnectedSpace (zmultiples p)] (hp : ¬ IsOfFinAddOrder p) (a : Multiplicative ℤ)
    (e : 𝕜) :
    (addCircleMulEquivInt hp a).1 e = e + a.toAdd • p

decls.name: TauCeti.Deck.addCircleMulEquivInt_symm_zsmul_apply_zero
decls.statement:
theorem addCircleMulEquivInt_symm_zsmul_apply_zero [PreconnectedSpace 𝕜]
    [TotallyDisconnectedSpace (zmultiples p)] (hp : ¬ IsOfFinAddOrder p)
    (φ : Deck ((↑) : 𝕜 → AddCircle p)) :
    ((addCircleMulEquivInt hp).symm φ).toAdd • p = φ.1 0

decls.name: BasedPath
decls.doc: The compact-open based-path space out of `x₀`.
decls.statement: def BasedPath (x₀ : X)

decls.name: BasedPath.instTopologicalSpace
decls.statement: instance : TopologicalSpace (BasedPath x₀)

decls.name: BasedPath.endpoint
decls.doc: The endpoint of a based path.
decls.statement: def endpoint (γ : BasedPath x₀) : X

decls.name: BasedPath.continuous_endpoint
decls.doc: The endpoint map from based paths to their terminal point is continuous.
decls.statement: theorem continuous_endpoint : Continuous (endpoint (x₀ := x₀))

decls.name: BasedPath.toPath
decls.doc: View a based path as a path to its endpoint.
decls.statement: def toPath (γ : BasedPath x₀) : Path x₀ (endpoint γ)

decls.name: BasedPath.endpoint_def
decls.doc:
Definitional unfolding of `endpoint`. Not a global simp lemma: it overlaps with
`endpoint_refl` (and other `endpoint_…` lemmas) on the simp normal form, so we instead include it
explicitly in `simp [endpoint_def, …]` at each site that wants to bridge between the named
`endpoint γ = u` API and the underlying `γ.1 1` evaluation.
decls.statement: theorem endpoint_def (γ : BasedPath x₀) : endpoint γ = γ.1 1

decls.name: BasedPath.toPath_apply
decls.statement: theorem toPath_apply (γ : BasedPath x₀) (t : I) : toPath γ t = γ.1 t

decls.name: BasedPath.toPath_source
decls.statement: theorem toPath_source (γ : BasedPath x₀) : toPath γ 0 = x₀

decls.name: BasedPath.toPath_target
decls.statement: theorem toPath_target (γ : BasedPath x₀) : toPath γ 1 = endpoint γ

decls.name: BasedPath.ext
decls.statement: theorem ext {γ γ' : BasedPath x₀} (h : ∀ t, γ.1 t = γ'.1 t) : γ = γ'

decls.name: BasedPath.ofPath
decls.doc:
The canonical inclusion `Path x₀ y → BasedPath x₀`: package an ordinary path out of `x₀` as a
based path, forgetting `y` at the type level. The endpoint is recovered as
`endpoint (ofPath γ) = y` via `endpoint_ofPath`. The map `toPath` is a partial inverse:
`ofPath γ.toPath = γ` (`ofPath_toPath_self`), and conversely `(ofPath γ).toPath` is `γ` with its
right endpoint cast to `endpoint (ofPath γ)` (`toPath_ofPath`).
decls.statement: def ofPath {y : X} (γ : Path x₀ y) : BasedPath x₀

decls.name: BasedPath.toPath_ofPath
decls.statement:
theorem toPath_ofPath {y : X} (γ : Path x₀ y) :
    (ofPath γ).toPath = γ.cast rfl γ.target

decls.name: BasedPath.endpoint_ofPath
decls.statement: theorem endpoint_ofPath {y : X} (γ : Path x₀ y) : endpoint (ofPath γ) = y

decls.name: BasedPath.ofPath_toPath_self
decls.doc: The round-trip `ofPath ∘ toPath` is the identity on `BasedPath x₀`.
decls.statement: theorem ofPath_toPath_self (γ : BasedPath x₀) : ofPath γ.toPath = γ

decls.name: BasedPath.ofPath_cast
decls.doc: `ofPath` is invariant under reindexing the right endpoint via `Path.cast`.
decls.statement:
theorem ofPath_cast {y y' : X} (γ : Path x₀ y) (h : y' = y) :
    ofPath (γ.cast rfl h) = ofPath γ

decls.name: BasedPath.refl
decls.doc: The constant based path at `x₀`.
decls.statement: def refl (x₀ : X) : BasedPath x₀

decls.name: BasedPath.endpoint_refl
decls.statement: theorem endpoint_refl (x₀ : X) : endpoint (refl x₀) = x₀

decls.name: BasedPath.toPath_refl
decls.statement:
theorem toPath_refl (x₀ : X) :
    (refl x₀).toPath = Path.refl x₀

decls.name: BasedPath.ofPath_refl
decls.statement:
theorem ofPath_refl (x₀ : X) :
    ofPath (Path.refl x₀) = refl x₀

decls.name: BasedPath.append
decls.doc:
Append a path `δ` at the endpoint of a based path `γ`, defined as
`ofPath (γ.toPath.trans δ)`: the half `s ∈ [0, ½]` traverses `γ` at double speed and the half
`s ∈ [½, 1]` traverses `δ` at double speed (`Path.trans_apply`). The new endpoint is the endpoint
of `δ` (`endpoint_append`). This is the move used by `joinedIn_preimage_of_append` to slide a
based path within a path component of `endpoint ⁻¹' U`.
decls.statement:
def append {y : X} (γ : BasedPath x₀)
    (δ : Path (endpoint γ) y) : BasedPath x₀

decls.name: BasedPath.toPath_append
decls.statement:
theorem toPath_append {y : X} (γ : BasedPath x₀) (δ : Path (endpoint γ) y) :
    (append γ δ).toPath = (γ.toPath.trans δ).cast rfl (γ.toPath.trans δ).target

decls.name: BasedPath.endpoint_append
decls.statement:
theorem endpoint_append {y : X} (γ : BasedPath x₀) (δ : Path (endpoint γ) y) :
    endpoint (append γ δ) = y

decls.name: BasedPath.terminalTail
decls.doc:
The tail of a based path past time `a`, viewed as a `Path (γ.toPath.extend a) u` where
`u = endpoint γ`. Concretely it is `γ.toPath.truncateOfLE` between `a` and `1`, cast on the right
to land at `u`; the only hypothesis required is `a ≤ 1` (for `a < 0` the source is clamped
through `Path.extend`). This is the "compressed tail" piece used by `deformTerminal` to splice
a new endpoint path onto `γ` while preserving its image on `[0, a]`.

decls.name: BasedPath.deformTerminal
decls.doc:
Replace the terminal interval of a based path by first traversing a compressed tail of the
original path and then a new endpoint path.

decls.name: BasedPath.deformTerminal_apply
decls.doc:
Application lemma for `deformTerminal`: the spliced path is the three-branch `dite` selected
by `t ≤ a` and `t ≤ b`.
decls.statement:
theorem deformTerminal_apply {u v : X} (γ : BasedPath x₀) (hu : endpoint γ = u)
    (δ : Path u v) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hab : a < b) (hb : b < 1) (t : I) :
    (deformTerminal γ hu δ ha hab hb).1 t =
      if _ : (t : ℝ) ≤ a then γ.toPath.extend t else
        if _ : (t : ℝ) ≤ b then
          (terminalTail γ hu a (by linarith)).extend (((t : ℝ) - a) / (b - a))
        else δ.extend (((t : ℝ) - b) / (1 - b))

decls.name: BasedPath.deformTerminal_apply_of_le
decls.statement:
theorem deformTerminal_apply_of_le {u v : X} (γ : BasedPath x₀) (hu : endpoint γ = u)
    (δ : Path u v) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hab : a < b) (hb : b < 1)
    (t : I) (ht : (t : ℝ) ≤ a) :
    (deformTerminal γ hu δ ha hab hb).1 t = γ.toPath.extend t

decls.name: BasedPath.deformTerminal_apply_of_lt_of_le
decls.statement:
theorem deformTerminal_apply_of_lt_of_le {u v : X} (γ : BasedPath x₀)
    (hu : endpoint γ = u) (δ : Path u v) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hab : a < b) (hb : b < 1)
    (t : I) (hta : a < (t : ℝ)) (htb : (t : ℝ) ≤ b) :
    (deformTerminal γ hu δ ha hab hb).1 t =
      (terminalTail γ hu a (by linarith)).extend (((t : ℝ) - a) / (b - a))

decls.name: BasedPath.deformTerminal_apply_of_lt
decls.statement:
theorem deformTerminal_apply_of_lt {u v : X} (γ : BasedPath x₀) (hu : endpoint γ = u)
    (δ : Path u v) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hab : a < b) (hb : b < 1)
    (t : I) (ht : b < (t : ℝ)) :
    (deformTerminal γ hu δ ha hab hb).1 t = δ.extend (((t : ℝ) - b) / (1 - b))

decls.name: BasedPath.endpoint_deformTerminal
decls.doc: The endpoint of `deformTerminal γ hu δ ha hab hb` is the endpoint of `δ`.
decls.statement:
theorem endpoint_deformTerminal {u v : X} (γ : BasedPath x₀) (hu : endpoint γ = u)
    (δ : Path u v) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hab : a < b) (hb : b < 1) :
    endpoint (deformTerminal γ hu δ ha hab hb) = v

decls.name: BasedPath.continuous_append_initialSegmentFamily
decls.doc:
Appending a fixed terminal path's initial-segment family to a fixed based path is jointly
continuous in the family parameter. This packages the boilerplate for using
`Path.trans_continuous_family` to lift `append γ ∘ Path.initialSegmentFamily δ` to a continuous
map `I → BasedPath x₀`.

decls.name: BasedPath.exists_endpointNeighborhood_of_basicNeighborhood
decls.doc:
Extract an open path-connected endpoint neighborhood and a terminal interval avoiding the
subbasic compact sets that do not contain `1`.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_endpointNeighborhood_of_basicNeighborhood [LocallyPathConnectedSpace X]
    {x₀ : X} (γ : BasedPath x₀) (Tgood Tbad : Finset (Set I × Set X))
    (hTgood_open_mem : ∀ KU ∈ Tgood, IsOpen KU.2 ∧ endpoint γ ∈ KU.2)
    (hTbad_closed : ∀ KU ∈ Tbad, IsClosed KU.1)
    (hTbad_not_mem : ∀ KU ∈ Tbad, (1 : I) ∉ KU.1) :
    ∃ (W : Set X) (a₀ : I) (a b : ℝ),
      IsOpen W ∧ endpoint γ ∈ W ∧ IsPathConnected W ∧
      (∀ KU ∈ Tgood, W ⊆ KU.2) ∧
      Set.Ioc a₀ 1 ⊆ γ.toPath ⁻¹' W ∩ ⋂ KU ∈ Tbad, KU.1ᶜ ∧
      ((a₀ : I) : ℝ) < a ∧ 0 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ 1 ∧ a < b ∧ b < 1

decls.name: BasedPath.terminalTail_range_subset
decls.doc:
The range of the compressed terminal tail `terminalTail γ rfl a ha1` is contained in `W`,
given that the terminal interval `Set.Ioc a₀ 1` maps into `W` under `γ.toPath` (`hpreim`), that
`a₀ < a` (`ha₀_lt_a`) and that `a ≤ 1` (`ha1`). The tail retraces `γ` over `[a, 1]`, and every
such time already lies in `Set.Ioc a₀ 1`, so its image lies in `W`.
decls.statement:
theorem terminalTail_range_subset (γ : BasedPath x₀) {W : Set X} {a₀ : I} {a : ℝ}
    (hpreim : Set.Ioc a₀ 1 ⊆ γ.toPath ⁻¹' W)
    (ha₀_lt_a : ((a₀ : I) : ℝ) < a) (ha1 : a ≤ 1) :
    Set.range (terminalTail γ rfl a ha1) ⊆ W

decls.name: BasedPath.deformTerminal_apply_mem_of_lt
decls.doc:
For a time `t` with `a < t`, the deformed based path `deformTerminal γ rfl δ ha0 hab hb1`
takes a value in `U` at `t`, provided `W ⊆ U` (`hWU`), the terminal tail's range lies in `W`
(`htail`), and `δ`'s range lies in `W` (`hδW`). The bounds are `0 ≤ a` (`ha0`), `a < b` (`hab`),
`b < 1` (`hb1`), and `a ≤ 1` (`ha1`, which names the tail's defining bound). On `a < t ≤ b` the
value lies on the tail, and on `b < t` it lies on `δ`; either way it is in `W ⊆ U`.
decls.statement:
theorem deformTerminal_apply_mem_of_lt {v : X} (γ : BasedPath x₀)
    (δ : Path (endpoint γ) v) {W U : Set X} {a b : ℝ} (ha0 : 0 ≤ a) (hab : a < b) (hb1 : b < 1)
    (ha1 : a ≤ 1) (hWU : W ⊆ U) (htail : Set.range (terminalTail γ rfl a ha1) ⊆ W)
    (hδW : Set.range δ ⊆ W) (t : I) (hat : a < (t : ℝ)) :
    (deformTerminal γ rfl δ ha0 hab hb1).1 t ∈ U

decls.name: BasedPath.coe_le_of_mem_Tbad
decls.doc:
A time `t` in the set `K` of a `Tbad` pair `(K, U)` (`hKUbad`, `ht`) satisfies
`(t : ℝ) ≤ a`, provided the terminal interval `Set.Ioc a₀ 1` avoids every `Tbad` set
(`hbad_avoid`) and `a₀ < a` (`ha₀_lt_a`). Were `(t : ℝ) > a`, then `a₀ < a < t ≤ 1` would place
`t` in `Set.Ioc a₀ 1`, contradicting that `t` lies in the avoided set `K`.

decls.name: BasedPath.mapsTo_deformTerminal
decls.doc:
The deformed based path `deformTerminal γ rfl δ ha0 hab hb1` maps the set `K` of a
pair `(K, U) ∈ S` (`hKU`) into `U`. Here `hγKU` says `γ.1` already maps `K` into `U`;
`hT_of_S` includes `S` into `T`;
`hTgood_iff` and `hTbad_iff` split `T` according to whether `1 ∈ K`; `hW_good` says `W` refines
every `Tgood` target; `hIoc` places `Set.Ioc a₀ 1` inside `γ.toPath ⁻¹' W` and away from the
`Tbad` sets; `ha₀_lt_a`, `ha0`, `ha1`, `hab`, `hb1` are the bounds `a₀ < a`, `0 ≤ a`, `a ≤ 1`,
`a < b`, `b < 1`; and `hδW` says `δ` stays in `W`. For `t ≤ a` the deformed path agrees with `γ`,
and for `a < t` the pair is forced to be `Tgood`, so the value lies in `W ⊆ U`.
decls.statement:
theorem mapsTo_deformTerminal {v : X} (γ : BasedPath x₀) (δ : Path (endpoint γ) v)
    {S : Set (Set I × Set X)} {T Tgood Tbad : Finset (Set I × Set X)}
    (hT_of_S : ∀ KU, KU ∈ S → KU ∈ T)
    (hTgood_iff : ∀ KU, KU ∈ Tgood ↔ KU ∈ T ∧ (1 : I) ∈ KU.1)
    (hTbad_iff : ∀ KU, KU ∈ Tbad ↔ KU ∈ T ∧ (1 : I) ∉ KU.1)
    {W : Set X} (hW_good : ∀ KU ∈ Tgood, W ⊆ KU.2) {a₀ : I} {a b : ℝ}
    (hIoc : Set.Ioc a₀ 1 ⊆ γ.toPath ⁻¹' W ∩ ⋂ KU ∈ Tbad, KU.1ᶜ)
    (ha₀_lt_a : ((a₀ : I) : ℝ) < a) (ha0 : 0 ≤ a) (ha1 : a ≤ 1) (hab : a < b) (hb1 : b < 1)
    (hδW : Set.range δ ⊆ W) {K : Set I} {U : Set X} (hKU : (K, U) ∈ S)
    (hγKU : Set.MapsTo γ.1 K U) :
    Set.MapsTo (deformTerminal γ rfl δ ha0 hab hb1).1 K U

decls.name: BasedPath.exists_deformTerminal_mem_basicNeighborhood
decls.doc:
Any point in the chosen path-connected endpoint neighborhood is realized by a deformed based
path that still lies in the original compact-open basic neighborhood.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_deformTerminal_mem_basicNeighborhood
    {x₀ : X} (γ : BasedPath x₀) {V : Set (C(I, X))} {S : Set (Set I × Set X)}
    {T Tgood Tbad : Finset (Set I × Set X)}
    (hSdata : ∀ K U, (K, U) ∈ S → IsCompact K ∧ IsOpen U ∧ Set.MapsTo γ.1 K U)
    (hT_of_S : ∀ KU, KU ∈ S → KU ∈ T)
    (hSV : {g : C(I, X) | ∀ K U, (K, U) ∈ S → Set.MapsTo g K U} ⊆ V)
    (hTgood_iff : ∀ KU, KU ∈ Tgood ↔ KU ∈ T ∧ (1 : I) ∈ KU.1)
    (hTbad_iff : ∀ KU, KU ∈ Tbad ↔ KU ∈ T ∧ (1 : I) ∉ KU.1)
    {W : Set X} (huW : endpoint γ ∈ W) (hWpath : IsPathConnected W)
    (hW_good : ∀ KU ∈ Tgood, W ⊆ KU.2)
    {a₀ : I} {a b : ℝ}
    (hIoc : Set.Ioc a₀ 1 ⊆ γ.toPath ⁻¹' W ∩ ⋂ KU ∈ Tbad, KU.1ᶜ)
    (ha₀_lt_a : ((a₀ : I) : ℝ) < a) (ha0 : 0 ≤ a) (ha1 : a ≤ 1) (hab : a < b) (hb1 : b < 1) :
    ∀ v ∈ W, ∃ η : BasedPath x₀, η.1 ∈ V ∧ endpoint η = v

decls.name: BasedPath.isOpenMap_endpoint
decls.doc: The endpoint map `BasedPath x₀ → X` is an open map when `X` is locally path-connected.
decls.statement:
theorem isOpenMap_endpoint [LocallyPathConnectedSpace X] (x₀ : X) :
    IsOpenMap (endpoint (x₀ := x₀))

decls.name: BasedPath.joinedIn_endpoint_preimage_of_homotopic
decls.doc:
Endpoint-preserving homotopic paths to a point `y ∈ U` give joined based paths inside the
endpoint preimage of `U`.

decls.name: BasedPath.joinedIn_preimage_of_append
decls.doc:
Appending a path that stays inside `U` moves a based path within the same path component of
the endpoint preimage of `U`.
decls.statement:
theorem joinedIn_preimage_of_append {U : Set X} {z : X} (γ : BasedPath x₀)
    (δ : Path (endpoint γ) z) (hδU : Set.range δ ⊆ U) :
    JoinedIn (endpoint (x₀ := x₀) ⁻¹' U) γ (append γ δ)

decls.name: BasedPath.exists_refined_terminal_vertex
decls.statement:
theorem exists_refined_terminal_vertex
    [LocallyPathConnectedSpace X]
    {x₀ : X} {n' : ℕ} {U : Set X} (hU_open : IsOpen U)
    (α : BasedPath x₀) (hα : endpoint α ∈ U)
    (part : IntervalPartition (n' + 1)) (T : TubeData X (n' + 1))
    (hα_tube : PathInTube α.toPath part T) :
    ∃ V_last' : Set X,
      IsOpen V_last' ∧ IsPathConnected V_last' ∧ endpoint α ∈ V_last' ∧
      V_last' ⊆ T.V (Fin.last (n' + 1)) ∧ V_last' ⊆ U

decls.name: BasedPath.isOpen_refined_tubeNeighborhood
decls.statement:
theorem isOpen_refined_tubeNeighborhood
    {x₀ : X} {n' : ℕ} (part : IntervalPartition (n' + 1))
    {U : Fin (n' + 1) → Set X} {V : Fin (n' + 2) → Set X}
    (hU_open : ∀ i, IsOpen (U i)) (hV_open : ∀ j, IsOpen (V j)) :
    IsOpen {β : BasedPath x₀ |
      (∀ (i : Fin (n' + 1)) (s : I),
          (part.t i.castSucc : ℝ) ≤ s ∧ s ≤ (part.t i.succ : ℝ) → β.1 s ∈ U i) ∧
      (∀ j, β.1 (part.t j) ∈ V j)}

decls.name: BasedPath.exists_refined_vertex_family
decls.doc:
**Refining the terminal vertex set of a tube.** If the last vertex set of `T` is replaced by a
smaller `V_last'` that is itself open, path-connected and contains `endpoint α`, the resulting
family is again open and path-connected, is contained in `T.V` pointwise, and `α` still passes
through it at every partition point.
decls.title: Refining the terminal vertex set of a tube
decls.statement:
theorem exists_refined_vertex_family {n' : ℕ} {part : IntervalPartition (n' + 1)}
    {T : TubeData X (n' + 1)} {α : BasedPath x₀}
    (hα_passes : ∀ j, α.toPath (part.t j) ∈ T.V j)
    {V_last' : Set X} (hV'_open : IsOpen V_last') (hV'_pathConn : IsPathConnected V_last')
    (hα_V' : endpoint α ∈ V_last') (hV'_sub_V : V_last' ⊆ T.V (Fin.last (n' + 1))) :
    ∃ V' : Fin (n' + 2) → Set X,
      (∀ j, IsOpen (V' j)) ∧ (∀ j, IsPathConnected (V' j)) ∧ (∀ j, V' j ⊆ T.V j) ∧
        V' (Fin.last (n' + 1)) = V_last' ∧ ∀ j, α.toPath (part.t j) ∈ V' j

decls.name: BasedPath.joinedIn_endpoint_preimage_of_pathInTube
decls.doc:
**A path through the refined tube is joined to `α`.** If `β` runs through the same tube as `α`
with refined vertex sets `V'` whose terminal member is contained in `U`, then `β` is joined to `α`
inside `endpoint ⁻¹' U`.
decls.title: A path through the refined tube is joined to `α`
decls.statement:
theorem joinedIn_endpoint_preimage_of_pathInTube {n' : ℕ} {U : Set X}
    {V' : Fin (n' + 2) → Set X} {part : IntervalPartition (n' + 1)}
    {T : TubeData X (n' + 1)} (hV'_open : ∀ j, IsOpen (V' j))
    (hV'_pathConn : ∀ j, IsPathConnected (V' j)) (hV'_sub_TV : ∀ j, V' j ⊆ T.V j)
    (hV'_last_sub_U : V' (Fin.last (n' + 1)) ⊆ U) {α β : BasedPath x₀}
    (hα_stays : ∀ (i : Fin (n' + 1)) (s : I),
      (part.t i.castSucc : ℝ) ≤ s ∧ s ≤ (part.t i.succ : ℝ) → α.toPath s ∈ T.U i)
    (hα_passes : ∀ j, α.toPath (part.t j) ∈ V' j)
    (hβ_stays : ∀ (i : Fin (n' + 1)) (s : I),
      (part.t i.castSucc : ℝ) ≤ s ∧ s ≤ (part.t i.succ : ℝ) → β.1 s ∈ T.U i)
    (hβ_passes : ∀ j, β.1 (part.t j) ∈ V' j) :
    JoinedIn (endpoint (x₀ := x₀) ⁻¹' U) α β

decls.name: BasedPath.exists_open_nhds_pathComponent_preimage
decls.doc:
Variable-endpoint tube/component theorem.

In a locally path-connected space, if semilocal simple connectivity holds along `α.toPath` and
`α : BasedPath x₀` has endpoint in an open set `U`, then `α` has an open neighborhood `N` in
`BasedPath x₀` such that every element of `N` has endpoint in `U` and lies in the same path
component of `endpoint ⁻¹' U` as `α`.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_open_nhds_pathComponent_preimage
    [LocallyPathConnectedSpace X] {U : Set X} (hU_open : IsOpen U)
    (α : BasedPath x₀) (hslsc : SemilocallySimplyConnectedOn (Set.range α.toPath))
    (hα : endpoint α ∈ U) :
    ∃ N : Set (BasedPath x₀), IsOpen N ∧ α ∈ N ∧
      N ⊆ endpoint (x₀ := x₀) ⁻¹' U ∧
      ∀ β ∈ N, JoinedIn (endpoint (x₀ := x₀) ⁻¹' U) α β

decls.name: BasedPath.isOpen_pathComponent_preimage
decls.doc: For an open neighborhood `U`, path components of `endpoint ⁻¹' U` are open.
decls.statement:
theorem isOpen_pathComponent_preimage
    [SemilocallySimplyConnectedSpace X] [LocallyPathConnectedSpace X]
    {U : Set X} (hU_open : IsOpen U) (α : BasedPath x₀) :
    IsOpen (pathComponentIn (endpoint (x₀ := x₀) ⁻¹' U) α)
